review_notes: I read the whole target file and the relevant parts of Uncrossing/Basic.lean: the UncrossStep definition, uncrossStep_iff and exists_uncross_cost_le. The file declares no simp lemmas or attributes. Its simp interface is therefore ad hoc calls on the raw Pi.single update formula. I did not find a rewrite cycle or a competing rule. I did not run Lean, so I make no claim about how simp behaves on these goals. The only finding is the missing evaluation lemma for the four-cell update. Settled and arms are private defs unfolded by name; I judged that acceptable.

findings.problem: The four-cell update is only available as the raw formula `B.toRealFun q = A.toRealFun q + δ * (Pi.single … q + Pi.single … q - Pi.single … q - Pi.single … q)`. There is no canonical simp lemma that evaluates it at a cell, in either `Basic` or this file. Each use therefore calls `rw [hB]` followed by a non-terminal `simp [Prod.mk.injEq, …]`, with disequalities supplied by hand. The same pattern appears at lines 78, 80, 84, 86, 115, 133 and 140. Those calls depend on how simp unfolds `Pi.single` on `ι × κ` into `if`/`Prod.mk.injEq` conditions. `Prod.mk.injEq` is already a simp lemma, so listing it is redundant. The tails are fragile, and some need `linarith` afterwards (lines 79 and 85).
findings.proposed_change: In `Uncrossing/Basic.lean`, add a small family of evaluation lemmas for the update, stated with `i₁ ≠ i₂` / `j₁ ≠ j₂` or `i₁ < i₂` / `j₁ < j₂`. They would cover the four corners and the off-corner case, e.g. `B.toRealFun (i₁, j₁) = A.toRealFun (i₁, j₁) + δ`, `B.toRealFun (i₁, j₂) = A.toRealFun (i₁, j₂) - δ`, and `B.toRealFun q = A.toRealFun q` when `q` is not one of the four corners. Each should be derived from the `Pi.single` hypothesis. Mark them `@[simp]` where the side conditions can be discharged, or state them as plain lemmas and call them with `simp only`. Then replace the repeated `rw [hB]; simp [Prod.mk.injEq, …]` blocks in `harm` and in the preservation part with `rw` or `simp only` calls to these lemmas.
findings.benefit: The update is normalised once to explicit cell values, instead of each call re-deriving the `Pi.single` case split with hand-fed disequalities. The proofs in `exists_pivot_step` become shorter and less sensitive to simp-set changes. Other consumers of `UncrossStep` get the same normal form.
